model_output.cross_horizon_summary: The 12h outlook is MIXED: BTC has stronger flow support, while ETH-relative weakness and near-term selling pressure leave participation vulnerable to fading. Neither the 72h nor 168h horizon has a defensible net directional edge. Current positive BTC ETF flows and broad absolute gains improve the picture relative to the structural prior, but do not establish sustained recovery or broad altcoin transmission. Pullback risk is elevated, not a confirmed decline or distribution signal. These are descriptive shadow forecasts with no portfolio execution authority.
global_missing_evidence: No independent sequence of recent breadth, relative-strength or order-flow observations establishes persistence. Zero deltas against the prior packet do not establish an unchanged market trajectory.
Canonical broad-alt and large-cap breadth remain UNCONFIRMED. Current breadth and capitalization buckets share an upstream source and must not receive independent votes.
The small-alt proxy covers only the Top-100 tail; the microcap universe is unavailable.
The latest supplied final ETF session is October 19, not the forecast's current session. Subsequent settled flow confirmation is unavailable.
Stablecoin supply is observed, but deployment into crypto risk assets is not established. Cross-venue persistent spot-demand and derivatives-positioning sequences are absent.

Catalyst context is degraded, macro observations are lagged, and the live-anchor source-observation freshness dimension is unavailable. These limitations reduce confidence rather than imply bearishness.

contradicting_evidence: Broad positive participation could support synchronized continuation: BTC and ETH gained approximately 2.36% and 2.31% over 24h, with 79 of 100 constituents advancing.
The latest settled BTC ETF inflow of $526.7 million provides meaningful upside counterevidence to a pullback interpretation, although it is not contemporaneous intraday demand.
Live funding rates are close to zero and hourly open interest fell for both assets; the packet does not establish an aggressively leveraged, crowded rally.
12h.expected_path: Uneven consolidation or a partial retracement of the 24h advance is more defensible than assuming synchronized continuation. BTC may remain relatively more resilient, while ETH and less-supported altcoins are more vulnerable to fading participation. The evidence does not support a precise turning time, price target or net market return.
falsification_conditions: Persistent gains across BTC and ETH, improving ETH/BTC, and sustained positive spot buying across subsequent observations would invalidate the near-term divergence-and-fade interpretation toward broader upside.
Persistent declines across BTC and ETH, contracting participation and continued sell-side pressure would invalidate the relative-resilience interpretation toward common downside.
missing_evidence: Repeated order-book and trade-flow observations are needed to distinguish persistent selling pressure from a transient single-venue snapshot.
The packet lacks a multi-hour price, volume and relative-strength sequence that could confirm continuation or a failed rebound.
Hourly funding-event rates are null; available live funding snapshots do not establish positioning changes.
supporting_evidence: The completed hourly candle shows BTC up approximately 0.09%, ETH down 0.12% and ETH/BTC down 0.24%, indicating near-term divergence despite positive 24h returns.

Hourly taker-buy quote shares were approximately 41.3% for BTC and 43.6% for ETH. The later Binance snapshot also shows strongly negative displayed depth imbalances and negative BTC taker imbalance, though ETH taker imbalance is approximately neutral.
BTC price rose while open interest fell approximately 1.16%; ETH price and open interest both fell. This does not establish fresh, broad-based speculative demand or durable spot-led recovery.
Filtered large-, mid- and small-alt proxy buckets have positive median returns, but fewer than half of each bucket outperform BTC. Absolute participation is stronger than relative leadership.

contradicting_evidence: An upside interpretation has substantive support from positive current breadth, positive filtered-bucket median returns, 90d altseason scores of 55 and 58, and the latest large BTC ETF inflow.
A downside interpretation has substantive support from weaker 30d relative participation, ETH ETF outflows, current ETH/BTC weakness and contracting 7d stablecoin supply.
168h.expected_path: No defensible week-long net direction is established. A recovery that broadens and a rebound that gives way to renewed weakness remain competing paths, not scheduled stages. Persistent joint improvement in prices, ETH/BTC, participation and settled flows would favor expansion; persistent joint deterioration would favor contraction. Neither is confirmed by this packet.
falsification_conditions: Repeated observations over the forecast window showing sustained price recovery, improving ETH/BTC, broad relative outperformance and supportive settled flows would resolve NO_EDGE toward UP.
Repeated observations showing failed recoveries, declining BTC and ETH, weakening relative participation and sustained adverse flows would resolve NO_EDGE toward DOWN.
missing_evidence: A current multi-session sequence of ETF flows, breadth, ETH/BTC and spot-demand measurements is needed to establish a weekly directional process.
Stablecoin deployment, broader small-cap participation and microcap transmission are not observed.
No reliable forward catalyst schedule or supported cycle-transition date is supplied.
supporting_evidence: Longer- and shorter-window relative participation conflict: the BlockchainCenter 90d score is 55, while its 30d score is 37 and the 30d median alt-minus-BTC return is negative.

The latest settled flow snapshot improves the BTC picture relative to the structural prior's negative five-session context, but ETH remains negative. Neither observation establishes a new persistent weekly flow regime.
Current broad absolute gains coexist with minority BTC outperformance across all observed capitalization buckets, leaving broad rotation unconfirmed.

A single current breadth observation and a single completed hourly candle cannot distinguish durable weekly recovery from a temporary rebound. The structural prior is context, not independent confirmation.

contradicting_evidence: An upside edge could emerge from the combination of strong absolute breadth, positive returns across filtered capitalization buckets and substantial latest-session BTC ETF inflows.
A downside edge could emerge if current ETH-relative weakness, negative ETH ETF flows and short-window stablecoin contraction persist alongside weakening prices.
Near-zero live funding and falling hourly open interest argue against treating the current advance as demonstrably leverage-driven excess.
72h.expected_path: Rebound extension and renewed testing of the recovery are both credible, without enough evidence to select the net 72h direction. BTC has better observed institutional-flow support than ETH, but that advantage does not establish continued BTC gains or transmission into altcoins. NO_EDGE does not imply a quiet or sideways market.
falsification_conditions: Sustained BTC and ETH gains accompanied by stronger ETH/BTC, persistent relative breadth and additional supportive settled flows would resolve the uncertainty toward UP.
Failed recovery attempts accompanied by persistent BTC and ETH declines, weaker participation and adverse settled flows would resolve the uncertainty toward DOWN.
missing_evidence: No current multi-session sequence confirms whether the latest BTC inflow and ETH outflow persist or reverse.
Only one settled BTC-dominance level is supplied; no dominance trend can be inferred.
Repeated breadth, ETH/BTC and spot-demand measurements are needed to test whether the 24h advance develops into persistent expansion.
supporting_evidence: Latest settled ETF flows are sharply split: BTC received $526.7 million while ETH lost $103.3 million. Their aggregate is positive, so the prior's negative-flow description cannot simply be carried forward.
Although 79% of the broad proxy advanced, only 36 of 100 constituents outperformed BTC and 37 outperformed ETH. This supports broad absolute gains without confirming broad relative leadership.
Stablecoin supply declined approximately 0.88% over 7d, but only approximately 0.10% over 30d, and deployment is unestablished. This limits liquidity confirmation without proving forced selling.
The available hourly ETH/BTC decline and short-term sell-side pressure conflict with the positive 24h breadth snapshot; neither has demonstrated persistence.
